Early [signs](/wiki/Medical_sign "Medical sign") and [symptoms](/wiki/Symptoms "Symptoms") of ovarian cancer may be absent or subtle. In most cases, symptoms exist for several months before being recognized and [diagnosed](/wiki/Diagnosis "Diagnosis").[[27]](#cite_note-Harrisons-27)[[28]](#cite_note-CDCsep2016-28) Symptoms can often be misdiagnosed as [irritable bowel syndrome](/wiki/Irritable_bowel_syndrome "Irritable bowel syndrome").[[29]](#cite_note-Jayson-29) The early stages of ovarian cancer tend to be painless which makes it difficult to detect it early on. Symptoms can vary based on the subtype.[[27]](#cite_note-Harrisons-27) Ovarian [borderline tumors](/wiki/Borderline_tumor "Borderline tumor"), also known as low malignant potential (LMP) ovarian tumors, do not cause an increase in [CA125](/wiki/CA125 "CA125") levels and are not identifiable with an ultrasound. The typical symptoms of an LMP tumor can include [abdominal distension](/wiki/Abdominal_distension "Abdominal distension") or pelvic pain. Particularly large masses tend to be benign or borderline.[[30]](#cite_note-Hoffman35-30)[[27]](#cite_note-Harrisons-27)

As Indonesia's capital, Jakarta is one of Southeast Asia's main diplomatic centres. The city's regional role stems from its position as the political centre of ASEAN's largest member state,[[351]](#cite_note-354) the presence of numerous [foreign embassies](/wiki/Diplomatic_mission "Diplomatic mission"), the ASEAN Headquarters, and the permanent missions of ASEAN member states and dialogue partners.[[181]](#cite_note-Salmande-184) Taken together, these institutions make Jakarta a regular venue for regional diplomacy, economic coordination, and ASEAN-related meetings.[[181]](#cite_note-Salmande-184)

Jakarta also participates in international city networks focused on climate policy, smart-city governance, and urban cooperation. The city has been a member of the [C40 Cities network](/wiki/C40_Cities_Climate_Leadership_Group "C40 Cities Climate Leadership Group") since 2006[[352]](#cite_note-355) and is part of the [ASEAN Smart Cities Network](/wiki/ASEAN_Smart_Cities_Network "ASEAN Smart Cities Network");[[353]](#cite_note-356) it also took part in the [Asian Network of Major Cities 21](/wiki/Asian_Network_of_Major_Cities_21 "Asian Network of Major Cities 21"), an earlier inter-city forum that remained active until 2014. **Telephone numbers in the People's Republic of China** are administered according to the Telecommunications Network Numbering Plan of China. The structure of [telephone numbers](/wiki/Telephone_number "Telephone number") for landlines and mobile service is different. Landline telephone numbers have area codes, whereas mobile numbers do not. In major cities, landline numbers consist of a two-digit area code followed by an eight-digit local number. In other places, landline numbers consist of a three-digit area code followed by a seven- or eight-digit local number. Mobile phone numbers consist of eleven digits.

Landline calls within the same area do not require the area code. Calls to other areas require dialing the trunk prefix *0* and the area code.

The [special administrative regions](/wiki/Special_administrative_regions_of_China "Special administrative regions of China") of [Hong Kong](/wiki/Hong_Kong "Hong Kong") and [Macau](/wiki/Macau "Macau") are not part of this numbering plan, and use the calling codes [852](/wiki/%2B852 "+852") and [853](/wiki/%2B853 "+853") respectively.

The most massive of the moons are the four [Galilean moons](/wiki/Galilean_moons "Galilean moons"): [Io](/wiki/Io_(moon) "Io (moon)"), [Europa](/wiki/Europa_(moon) "Europa (moon)"), [Ganymede](/wiki/Ganymede_(moon) "Ganymede (moon)"), and [Callisto](/wiki/Callisto_(moon) "Callisto (moon)"), all of which were independently discovered in 1610 by [Galileo Galilei](/wiki/Galileo_Galilei "Galileo Galilei") and [Simon Marius](/wiki/Simon_Marius "Simon Marius") and were [the first objects found](/wiki/Timeline_of_discovery_of_Solar_System_planets_and_their_moons "Timeline of discovery of Solar System planets and their moons") to orbit a body that was neither [Earth](/wiki/Earth "Earth") nor the [Sun](/wiki/Sun "Sun").
